answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a meaningful stake in a shared vault before it may transact; the stake is slashed if the agent misbehaves. New identities start on the lowest rung of a trust trellis, earning higher limits only through attested work over time, so spinning up thousands of fake accounts gains nothing. A registry can forge each identity from a verified hardware or social attestation, binding one keypair to one real entity. Creating many sybils then costs real collateral and time, making the attack uneconomical.
